source.title: Depth Improves Training-Time Scaling for Difficult Tasks in Deep Linear Networks
source.authors: Taishi Watanabe; Ryo Karakida; Jun-nosuke Teramae

record.file_problem: The full paper, including appendices, is present. Some equation and figure text has minor extraction artifacts, but the relevant results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study derives and tests how task spectrum and network depth affect training-time loss scaling in deep linear networks, refining a prior depth-independent prediction for that setting. It does not test language-model pretraining scaling.
record.gate_note: The study reports results for population squared-loss regression, not held-out language-model pretraining loss. Its comparisons of depths use fixed widths, not fixed parameter counts. It does not test parameter/token/compute scaling or compute-optimal allocation. The predictor-norm and reparameterized-time analyses are included where they directly characterize the scaling result; cited findings from prior work are not recorded as study results.
record.test_reason: This is a theory paper on how training-time loss exponents depend on task spectrum and depth in deep linear regression networks, with small ReLU-MLP and CIFAR-derived linear-regression checks. It cites Kaplan and Hoffmann only as motivation. It never measures held-out language-model pretraining loss against parameters, tokens or compute. It fits no published LM scaling law and has no LM data, schedule or parameter-counting choices. No row measures what any version names for the kind of system the versions name, so none of its results tests a version. The depth- and spectrum-dependence of the training-time exponent is recorded under fits_no_version, as a related construct in a toy system.
record.authors_conclusion: Essentially correct. The authors also say the nonlinear ReLU distinction is less pronounced than in deep linear networks. They also state that the theory is limited to a linear teacher and student, population gradient flow, and, for standard initialization, difficult tasks only.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes supervised power-law regression with deep linear networks, population gradient flow, and some gradient-descent or SGD experiments. It does not use language models, held-out pretraining loss, parameter/token/compute scaling sweeps, or compute-optimal allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: The training-time exponent depends on task exponent p and depth L in the p < 1 regime; at p = 1 depth changes a logarithmic correction, and at p > 1 the power-law exponent is depth-independent. Finite input dimension delays the fitted asymptotic behavior, especially at greater depth. The standard-initialization theorem is limited to p < 1.

fits_no_version.finding: In deep linear networks under gradient flow, the training-time loss exponent is pL/[1+p(L-1)] for p<1, rising with depth. At p=1 only a log correction depends on depth, and for p>1 the exponent is depth-independent. Fig 4 fits at d=2048 match theory, with seed SD at most ~0.004.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-time loss exponents in factorized linear models depend jointly on the task spectrum and on depth.

fits_no_version.finding: At finite input dimension, fitted exponents approach the asymptotic values only slowly, more slowly for deeper networks. Exponents fitted at moderate size can therefore differ from the asymptotic ones.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Finite-size effects bias fitted training-time exponents, especially in deeper models.

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR-derived linear regression (peff≈0.478), the loss decays faster with depth. In ReLU MLPs, depth lowers late-time loss for p=0.6 but not for p=1.4. Single seeds, figure only.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The task-dependent depth effect on training-time scaling partly carries over beyond linear theory.

record.problems: The central theory assumes a linear teacher and student and population gradient flow. Standard-initialization theory is limited to difficult tasks. The extensions are qualitative: the CIFAR-derived runs and each ReLU curve use a single random initialization, and their results are mainly shown in figures. The study does not test language-model pretraining or compute-optimal allocation.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported results bearing on V7 were left out. The predictor-norm growth results were not entered as rows because they do not directly measure the version's fitted loss exponents.

untested.parts: No language-model pretraining loss against parameters, tokens or compute. Only training-time loss in linear regression.
No extrapolation from small to large runs.
Depth is varied at fixed width, not at fixed parameter count, and not in language models.
No image or video models, repeated data, fine-tuning or transfer. The CIFAR task is linear regression on pixels.
No published LM laws, parameter counting, schedules, LM data or fitting methods are compared. The exponent dependence shown is on task spectrum and depth in a toy model.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V7 link stretches the version. V7 concerns setup- and fit-dependence of published LM scaling laws, whereas this study is toy-model theory with training time as the resource. Fig 4's numeric exponent fits are not rowed, but no version needs them. Row r7's settings were copied from Figs 1-3.

versions.untested_parts: The study measures population squared loss versus training time in supervised regression, not held-out language-model pretraining loss versus parameter count, tokens, or compute.
No small-run fits are used to predict much larger language-model runs.
The study does not optimize parameter and token allocation under a fixed compute budget.
Depth is varied, but the study does not compare architectures at a fixed parameter count or establish that architecture details change loss only slightly.
The CIFAR-derived task is supervised linear regression, not an image-model scaling-law test; repeated data, fine-tuning, transfer, and other modalities or regimes are not tested.
No downstream task performance is measured.

The study varies task spectrum, depth, initialization, dimension, and fitting window, but does not vary parameter-counting conventions, training schedules systematically, fitting methods, or language-model data setups. It does not test compute-optimal allocation.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Deep linear population-gradient-flow setting, varying task exponent and depth; finite-dimension fitting results
reader_labels.reason: The derived training-time exponents vary with task regime and, for p < 1, depth; the finite-dimension fits approach asymptotic predictions more slowly at greater depth (r1-r6).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The image-derived linear task shows a depth-related trend, but the nonlinear experiments show it qualitatively for p = 0.6 and no systematic late-time depth advantage for p = 1.4; each curve uses one random initialization (r7-r16).
